Title: Team Jacobs punches Olympic ticket with 6-5 win over Winnipeg's Dunstone

Summary: 
Team Brad Jacobs secured Canada's spot in the men's curling event at the 2026 Winter Olympics with a 6-5 victory over Matt Dunstone's Winnipeg team in the best-of-three final of the Canadian Olympic Curling Trials in Halifax. The win, decided in the 10th end with a perfect shot by Jacobs to the button, completed a sweep after Jacobs had won the first game 9-8 without throwing his final stone. Jacobs, third Marc Kennedy, second Brett Gallant, and lead Ben Hebert each have prior Olympic podium experience: Jacobs won gold in 2014, Kennedy and Hebert won gold in 2010 and silver in 2018, and Gallant earned bronze in 2022. Gallant will also compete in the mixed doubles event with his wife, Jocelyn Peterman. Team Jacobs is ranked No. 3 globally, having won the 2025 Brier and earned bronze at the 2025 World Championships. Earlier on the same day, Rachel Homan’s Ottawa team won the women’s Olympic berth with a 12-3 sweep over Christina Black’s Halifax rink. The 2026 Winter Olympics will be held in Milano Cortina, Italy, in February.

Title: Ready for a trip to the 'park? Snowboarding set for its spotlight at the Winter Olympics

Summary: 
Snowboarding is set to shine at the 2026 Winter Olympics, with five events across two disciplines: park (halfpipe, slopestyle, big air) and racing (snowboardcross, parallel giant slalom). The park events are judged based on trick complexity and aerial height, while snowboardcross features four-rider races down winding courses and parallel giant slalom resembles Alpine skiing. Key athletes to watch include Chloe Kim, aiming for a historic third consecutive halfpipe title despite a shoulder injury; Ayumu Hirano of Japan, seeking a repeat in the halfpipe; Australian Scotty James, a top contender against Hirano; and Czech Republic’s Esther Ledecka, the two-time defending parallel giant slalom champion. American Red Gerard, the 2018 slopestyle gold medalist, is in strong form and aiming for a podium return after finishing fourth in Beijing. Events will take place at Livigno Snow Park from February 5 to 18, with big air (Feb 5–9), parallel giant slalom (Feb 8), halfpipe (Feb 11–13), snowboardcross (Feb 13–15), and slopestyle (Feb 16–18). The sport’s Olympic debut was in 1998, and it gained global attention in 2002 when Ross Powers, Danny Kass, and JJ Thomas swept the halfpipe podium. Shaun White’s 2018 gold in a narrow win over Hirano remains one of the most dramatic moments, and he retired after a fourth-place finish in 2022. A notable early moment involved Ross Rebagliati, who won gold in 1998 but had it stripped after testing positive for cannabis—later reinstated on appeal.

Published date: January 08 2026, 22:12
